title: Initial-horn cylinder pushout of a marked mapping simplex
statement:
Use small simplicial sets, simplices, horns and degreewise products of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], the marked mapping simplex of [lem-coef-cartesian-mapping-simplex-presentation], and marked products and minimal markings of [lem-coef-marked-point-cartesian-model]. Let $n\geq1$ and let $A_0\leftarrow\cdots\leftarrow A_n$ be a chain of small simplicial sets, with transition maps $t_{j,i}:A_j\to A_i$ for $i\leq j$. Put $M=M^m(A)$, whose $r$-simplices are $(\alpha,a)$ with $\alpha:[r]\to[n]$ monotone and $a\in(A_{\alpha(r)})_r$, and put $K=\Lambda_0^n$ and $M_K=M\times_{\Delta^n}K$. Let $T_n$ consist of all degenerate edges of $\Delta^n$ and the edge $[0,1]$. Give $M$ the marking in which $(\alpha,a)$ is marked exactly when $\alpha\in T_n$ and $a$ is degenerate, and give $M_K$ the induced marking. Write $K^T=(K,T_n\cap K_1)$ and $D^T=(\Delta^n,T_n)$. The formula
$$c:A_n^\flat\times D^T\longrightarrow M,\qquad (a,\alpha)\longmapsto(\alpha,t_{n,\alpha(r)}(a))$$
defines a marked simplicial map. It restricts to $c_K:A_n^\flat\times K^T\to M_K$, and $c_K$ and the product inclusion exhibit $M$ as the pushout of the span
$$M_K\xleftarrow{c_K}A_n^\flat\times K^T\longrightarrow A_n^\flat\times D^T,$$
with structure maps the inclusion $M_K\to M$ and $c$. Explicitly, this is a pushout in marked simplicial sets: for every marked simplicial set $Z$, compatible marked maps from $M_K$ and $A_n^\flat\times D^T$ to $Z$ extend uniquely to a marked map $M\to Z$. This includes $n=1$, where $K=\{0\}$ and $M_K=A_0^\flat$, and allows empty terms of the chain.

proof.text:
For a monotone $\theta:[s]\to[r]$, the mapping-simplex operator gives
$$\theta^*c_r(a,\alpha)=(\alpha\theta,t_{\alpha(r),\alpha\theta(s)}\theta^*t_{n,\alpha(r)}a)=(\alpha\theta,t_{n,\alpha\theta(s)}\theta^*a)=c_s(\theta^*a,\alpha\theta).$$
The middle equality uses only that the transition maps are simplicial and $t_{j,i}t_{n,j}=t_{n,i}$. Thus $c$ is simplicial. A marked product edge has $a=s_0b$ and $\alpha\in T_n$; its image has second coordinate $s_0t_{n,\alpha(1)}b$ and the same base edge, so is marked. Degenerate edges of $M$ have constant base and degenerate second coordinate, hence are included in its prescribed marking. Since $c$ preserves the base coordinate, its restriction $c_K$ lands in $M_K$ and is marked, and the displayed square commutes.

source.place: Section 3.2.2, printed p. 179, mapping-simplex operators; proof of Corollary 3.2.2.12, printed p. 186, reduction for i<n. The coordinate verification and selected-marking check here are agent-written expansions.

proof.text: By the stated definition of a horn, $\alpha:[r]\to[n]$ belongs to $K_r$ if and only if its image omits a vertex in $\{1,\ldots,n\}$. Consequently $\alpha\notin K_r$ forces $n$ into its image and, by monotonicity, $\alpha(r)=n$. Over every such $\alpha$, an $r$-simplex of $M$ is therefore $(\alpha,a)$ with $a\in(A_n)_r$, and $c_r(a,\alpha)=(\alpha,a)$ because $t_{n,n}=\mathrm{id}$. Thus $c$ is bijective on simplices outside the horn restriction. Its inverse image of $M_K$ is exactly $A_n\times K$, since it preserves the base. No injectivity of $c_K$ is asserted or needed.

source.place: Section 3.2.2, printed p. 179, mapping-simplex operators; proof of Corollary 3.2.2.12, printed p. 186, reduction for i<n. The coordinate verification and selected-marking check here are agent-written expansions.

proof.text: Fix a marked simplicial set $Z$ and compatible marked maps $u:M_K\to Z$ and $v:A_n^\flat\times D^T\to Z$, so $u c_K=v|_{A_n\times K}$. Define functions $h_r:M_r\to Z_r$ by $h_r(\alpha,a)=u_r(\alpha,a)$ when $\alpha\in K_r$, and by $h_r(\alpha,a)=v_r(a,\alpha)$ when $\alpha\notin K_r$. In the second case $a\in(A_n)_r$ by Step 2, so this is defined. These functions restrict to $u$. For any $(b,\alpha)\in(A_n)_r\times(\Delta^n)_r$, if $\alpha\in K_r$, compatibility gives $h_rc_r(b,\alpha)=u_rc_{K,r}(b,\alpha)=v_r(b,\alpha)$; otherwise $c_r(b,\alpha)=(\alpha,b)$ and the same equality follows from the definition. Hence $h c=v$ degree by degree, even when several cylinder simplices have the same image over $K$.

source.place: Section 3.2.2, printed p. 179, mapping-simplex operators; proof of Corollary 3.2.2.12, printed p. 186, reduction for i<n. The coordinate verification and selected-marking check here are agent-written expansions.

proof.text:
The functions $h_r$ commute with every simplicial operator. Indeed, for $x\in(M_K)_r$, also $\theta^*x\in(M_K)_s$, and $h_s(\theta^*x)=u_s(\theta^*x)=\theta^*u_r(x)=\theta^*h_r(x)$. Every remaining $x\in M_r$ has the form $c_r(b,\alpha)$ by Step 2. Using Step 1 and the degreewise identity $h c=v$ from Step 3 gives
$$h_s(\theta^*x)=h_sc_s(\theta^*b,\alpha\theta)=v_s(\theta^*b,\alpha\theta)=\theta^*v_r(b,\alpha)=\theta^*h_r(x).$$
This includes operators whose image enters the horn. Thus $h$ is a simplicial map extending both given maps.

source.place: Section 3.2.2, printed p. 179, mapping-simplex operators; proof of Corollary 3.2.2.12, printed p. 186, reduction for i<n. The coordinate verification and selected-marking check here are agent-written expansions.

proof.text: If a marked edge $e=(\alpha,a)$ of $M$ lies in $M_K$, its image under $h$ is marked since $u$ is marked and the marking on $M_K$ is induced. Otherwise Step 2 gives $\alpha(1)=n$, and $a$ is degenerate by the marking prescribed in the statement. Since $\alpha\in T_n$, the edge $(a,\alpha)$ is marked in $A_n^\flat\times D^T$, and $h(e)=v(a,\alpha)$ is marked. Hence $h$ is a marked map. Any other extension equals $u$ on $M_K$ and equals $v$ on every image of $c$; these cover all simplices by Step 2, so it equals $h$ in every degree. This proves exactly the marked pushout universal property.

source.place: Section 3.2.2, printed p. 179, mapping-simplex operators; proof of Corollary 3.2.2.12, printed p. 186, reduction for i<n. The coordinate verification and selected-marking check here are agent-written expansions.

proof.text: For $n=1$, the horn criterion of Step 2 says that every simplex of $K$ is constant at $0$. Thus $K=\{0\}$, its mapping-simplex restriction has simplices precisely those of $A_0$, and its induced marking is exactly the degenerate edges: $M_K=A_0^\flat$. The construction above therefore gives the asserted marked mapping-cylinder pushout also in this case. All constructions are formulas on existing simplices; none selects a vertex in a term of the chain. In particular if $A_n$ is empty there are no simplices outside $M_K$, so the same extension formula still works, and arbitrary empty terms require no additional assumption.

Step 1: c is simplicial because the transitions compose, and it is marked. The prescribed marking on M contains the degenerate edges. Step 2: a simplex outside the initial horn hits {1..n}, so alpha(r)=n and c is a bijection there. Step 3: the piecewise h is well-typed and hc=v holds even when c_K is not injective. Step 4: naturality holds, including faces that enter the horn, with no circularity. Step 5: every marked edge outside M_K comes from a marked cylinder edge, and uniqueness follows from coverage, so this is the marked universal property, not an unmarked one. Step 6: n=1 gives M_K=A_0^flat, and empty A_n needs no choice. I tested n=1 (mapping cylinder with (Delta^1)^sharp), n=2 (faces of (012,a); no marked edges outside K) and a non-injective transition. lean.statement: theorem mapping_simplex_initial_horn_pushout {n : ℕ} (A : SimplexChain.{u} (n + 1)) : ∃ c : Marked.product (Marked.flat (A.obj (op (Fin.last (n + 1))))) (Marked.initialMarkedSimplex n) ⟶ initialEdgeMappingSimplex A, (∀ (r : SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ) (a : (A.obj (op (Fin.last (n + 1)))).obj r) (α : (Δ[n + 1] : SSet.{u}).obj r), c.val.app r (a, α) = ⟨stdSimplex.asOrderHom α, (A.map (homOfLE (Fin.le_last (stdSimplex.asOrderHom α (Fin.last r.unop.len)))).op).app r a⟩) ∧ ∃ cK : Marked.product (Marked.flat (A.obj (op (Fin.last (n + 1))))) (Marked.inducedMarking (Marked.initialMarkedSimplex n) (horn (n + 1) (0 : Fin (n + 2))).ι) ⟶ initialHornMappingSimplex A, IsPushout cK (Marked.productMap (𝟙 (Marked.flat (A.obj (op (Fin.last (n + 1)))))) (Marked.initialMarkedHorn n)) (Marked.inducedMarkingMap (initialEdgeMappingSimplex A) (initialHornMappingSimplexSubcomplex A).ι) c
lean.note: The existing chain and mapping simplex are reused. The three helper definitions give its selected marking and concrete inverse-image horn restriction. The theorem specifies the canonical cylinder map by its coordinates in every degree and asserts that its horn restriction gives a strict marked pushout, without fibrancy, nonemptiness or injectivity assumptions. Positive dimensions are parametrized as n + 1.
